original_question: Characterize exactly which graphs are rectangle visibility graphs, where vertices are isothetic rectangles with pairwise disjoint interiors and two vertices are adjacent exactly when their rectangles are horizontally or vertically visible by an unobstructed beam of finite width.
target_in_paper: Open Problem 27 in Section 3.3 (“Bar Visibility Graphs”): “Characterize rectangle visibility graphs.” ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s official target. It correctly asks for an exact characterization of rectangle visibility graphs and correctly captures the defining model immediately preceding Open Problem 27: isothetic rectangles, pairwise disjoint interiors, and adjacency defined exactly by horizontal or vertical unobstructed visibility of finite width. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
missing_details: The paper makes the rectangles explicitly closed and places them explicitly in the plane; those two details are implicit in your draft but not stated. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

To be fully stand-alone, the question should quantify over finite graphs G and ask which such graphs admit a rectangle-visibility representation of this exact type. That is the intended meaning of the paper’s terse formulation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
It is worth preserving the paper’s finite-width beam language so the problem does not drift toward a zero-width or strong-visibility variant. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

The scope should remain the ordinary rectangle-visibility model only, not nearby variants discussed in the same subsection or literature such as bar visibility, bar k-visibility, or unit bar/rectangle variants. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

No ambient ring, field, polynomial degree, homogeneity, nilpotency condition, or asymptotic phrase such as “for all sufficiently large m” is relevant here; the hidden formal content is purely the graph-theoretic quantifier and the exact visibility-representation conditions above. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
refined_question: Characterize exactly the finite graphs G that admit a rectangle visibility representation, namely, a realization of the vertices of G by closed isothetic rectangles in the plane with pairwise disjoint interiors such that two distinct vertices u and v are adjacent in G if and only if their corresponding rectangles are vertically or horizontally visible from each other by a beam of unobstructed visibility of finite width. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
justification: The draft clearly targets the unnumbered definition of rectangle visibility graphs and the immediately following Open Problem 27 in Section 3.3, rather than a broader neighboring recognition problem or another visibility model. The official problem statement itself is simply “Characterize rectangle visibility graphs,” while the surrounding paragraph supplies the missing formal content: closed isothetic rectangles in the plane, pairwise disjoint interiors, and horizontal/vertical visibility via an unobstructed finite-width beam. I therefore kept your scope unchanged and only made those paper-supplied conditions explicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
